description: agro run egress. ADR #1378 (Accepted) shipped the allowlist for the long-lived sandbox in mifunedev/agro#1398: `.devcontainer/docker-compose.egress.yml` puts the sandbox on an internal network behind a pinned `ubuntu/squid` proxy. `registry.ts` builds the host list from the OpenShell policy hosts plus `access.egressAllow`. ADR #1575 records open egress as a limit of `agro run` (mifunedev/agro#1580, #1585). This plan applies the same policy to `agro run`.

userStories.title: One allowlist source for the sandbox and agro run
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want one allowlist function and one proxy configuration so that the sandbox and `agro run` cannot drift apart.
acceptanceCriteria: `egressAllowHosts` moves from `.agro/cli/src/lib/registry.ts` to an exported function in `.agro/cli/src/lib/egress-policy.ts`, and `registry.ts` imports it.
A test proves that `EGRESS_SQUID_CONF` equals the `egress-squid` content in `.devcontainer/docker-compose.egress.yml`, and that `EGRESS_PROXY_IMAGE` equals the `proxy` image digest there.
`pnpm typecheck` exits 0, and `pnpm test` through `agro run` shows no new failure against `evidence/baseline.md`.
userStories.notes: executed (advisor, 7472088e, via agro run): typecheck 0; egress-policy.test.ts passes including the compose equality test; full suite shows only the baseline install.sh drift failure. reasoned: egressAllowHosts and policyHosts moved to egress-policy.ts and imported by registry.ts; EGRESS_SQUID_CONF and EGRESS_PROXY_IMAGE exported and pinned to the compose file by test.

userStories.title: agro run enforces the allowlist
userStories.description: As an operator, I want `agro run` to honor `access.egress: "allowlist"` so that an untrusted command reaches only allowed hosts.
acceptanceCriteria: When `access.egress` is `allowlist`, `agro run` creates an internal network `agro-run-<id>` (`docker network create --internal`) and an egress network `agro-run-<id>-out`.

`agro run` starts a proxy container from `EGRESS_PROXY_IMAGE` on both networks with the alias `proxy`. The proxy mounts `EGRESS_SQUID_CONF` and the `egressAllowHosts` list read-only from a temp directory.

The command container and each service join only the internal network. The command container receives `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `https_proxy`, `http_proxy`, `NO_PROXY`, `no_proxy`, and `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` with the values of the compose file.
`agro run` waits until the proxy accepts connections on port 3128, then runs the command.
After the command, and after a failure, `agro run` removes the proxy, each service, both networks, and the temp directory.
When `access.egress` is `open` or absent, the `docker` argument vectors do not change.
Tests assert the exact argument vectors and the removal order through a fake runner.
`pnpm typecheck` exits 0, and `pnpm test` through `agro run` shows no new failure against the baseline.

userStories.title: Documentation and changelog
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the egress behavior of `agro run` documented so that a project can rely on the allowlist.
acceptanceCriteria: The `agro run` section of `docs/lifecycle-commands.md` describes the allowlist mode, the proxy variables, and the internal network.
`CHANGELOG.md` holds one entry under `## [Unreleased]` that links the task issue.

userStories.title: Validation
userStories.description: As the operator, I want proof that the allowlist holds under `agro run` so that I can close the egress gap of ADR #1575.
acceptanceCriteria: `.agro/tasks/agro-run-egress/evidence/manual-review.md` records a scratch repository with `access.egress: "allowlist"` and `access.egressAllow: ["example.org"]`.
Through the proxy, a request to `https://example.org` returns HTTP 200, and a request to `https://example.com` fails with a proxy denial.
A direct request that bypasses the proxy fails, because the network is internal.
A declared `postgres` service stays reachable from the command.
After each run, `docker ps -a` and `docker network ls` show no `agro-run-` container or network, and the run deletes the scratch repository.
